2. open_threads:
THE UNRIPE PREDICATE, and it is worth a look tomorrow: the repaired probe's _enough has its promotion half already satisfied (3 earned nodes at 2 corroborating questions each) and is waiting only on decay — the oldest live row is 13 days against a 14-day DECAY_HORIZON, so it becomes evaluable roughly 2026-08-11. That is the first real efficacy answer the tenure loop will produce. would_trigger stays False at 9 crossings against a threshold of 20, which is a young tree standing down correctly.

THE HONEST GAP ON THE VOYAGE JUST CLOSED: done there was 'the instrument measures', NOT 'the tenure loop is healthy'. It closed green with the efficacy question still open. A reader who conflates them will think the tenure loop was validated on 2026-08-10; it was not.

TWO DESIGN QUESTIONS CARRIED FORWARD, neither validatable in that voyage and both recorded in the ticket: whether the two librarian probes should SHARE one tree name (coupling two instruments meant to be independent) rather than each holding its own correct literal that can drift again; and whether a probe should hold a hand-set tree constant AT ALL — blocked today by a measured absence, 15 tree-declaration sites across the librarian carrying 3 distinct values with no LIVE_TREE accessor and no charter field naming one. The second is the ticket's known_adjacent_debt and wants its own ticket.

A PROCESS BULLET FOR AKIEN: the seven-brick preamble ran for a one-constant repair. It was not wasted — survey is exactly where the MISAIMED falsifier died by measurement, and without that the fix would have been applied to a guess. But whether a bug door should carry the full chain is his call, and it now has one data point.

RECORDED HONESTLY RATHER THAN TIDIED: BUILDME on that voyage was journaled LATE and the journal says so. The earlier emit() was called without history_path/state_path and journaled nothing, so the build ran before the record moved — inverting the chokepoint's order. The crossing itself was legal (the entry gate read the validate berth); only its timing was wrong, and it was not backdated.

STILL UNTOUCHED BY DESIGN: `systemctl --user disable --now ground_loop.service` remains offered and NOT run — his host, his word. T4 (workflow-cursor-unreadable-by-the-chokepoint) needs his ratify to leave the live trouble list; CC's half is done.
